title: kv: fragment coordinator and lazy spill controller with workload-aware throttling
author: Maya Chen
description: Problem: We observed increasing KV cache fragmentation and frequent micro-evictions under mixed-length workloads which raised tail latency and I/O churn during spillover. Motivation: reduce CPU/IO overhead of eviction, reduce memory fragmentation, and keep serving latency within SLO when background reclamation kicks in. This PR introduces two coordinated components and scheduler hooks: 1) Fragment Coordinator - per-tenant lightweight tracker that maintains a moving histogram of allocation sizes, fragmentation score, and a prioritized compaction candidate queue. It exposes a soft budget and compaction score so the scheduler can decide when to run aggressive reclamation. 2) Lazy Spill Controller - groups small eviction candidates into batched spill requests and defers non-critical writes until a coalescing window. The controller is backpressure-aware: it will issue immediate spills when GPU memory pressure is high or when an explicit critical flag is set. Workload-aware throttling: integrates with runtime scheduler to adapt compaction and spill rates based on observed request P95/P99 and GPU free memory. If serving latency rises above configured SLO thresholds we temporarily reduce background compaction rate and prefer lightweight prefix-trimming evictions. Implementation notes: - New modules: kv/fragment_coordinator.rs, kv/lazy_spill_controller.rs, runtime/scheduler/eviction_policy_integration.rs - Metrics: kv.fragmentation_score{tenant}, kv.lazy_spill_coalesces, kv.background_compaction_seconds_total - Continuous batching integration: lazy spill controller uses continuous-batching shim to combine small writes before issuing disk/AIO ops - Fallbacks: if async compaction fails or times out, we force synchronous spill for safety - Config knobs: compaction_window_ms, spill_coalesce_window_ms, compaction_rate_limit, latency_slo_threshold Checklist: - [x] Design doc (internal link: linear/ENG-5128) - [x] Unit + integration tests for coordinator + controller - [x] Metrics and dashboard panels added - [x] Backwards-compatible config (defaults preserve current behavior) - [x] Perf microbenchmarks attached (see summary below) Perf summary: - Realistic mixed-length trace (60% short, 40% long KV entries) - Reduced small-spill IO ops by ~62% - Fragmentation score decreased by ~28% at steady state - End-to-end P99 serving latency improved by ~12% in presence of background reclamation Known limitations: - Compaction may be less effective on very small segments; we expose a compaction_threshold to tune. - The lazy coalesce window trades latency vs IO; default aims to be conservative for host workloads. Rollout plan: staged rollout: beta tenant => 10% production canary => 50% => global. Feature gated behind kv.fragment_reclaim.enabled. Related: touches scheduler, batching, and AIO layers—please review for cross-impact.
commits: 5 commits: 1) add fragment coordinator module + tests; 2) implement lazy spill controller + continuous-batching shim; 3) integrate eviction policy hooks into scheduler; 4) add metrics + dashboard mappings; 5) fix racy unit test and adjust default config

review_thread: Arjun: Can you explain how we avoid coordinating costly compaction across tenants? Maya: FragmentCoordinator keeps per-tenant soft budgets and only promotes to aggressive compaction when fragmentation_score > threshold AND node-wide free memory < pressure_threshold. We also limit concurrent compactions via compaction_rate_limit. Sofia: Need stronger guarantees around atomicity when coalescing spills (risk of partial failure). Maya: Added a write-group commit step and a retry path; if async coalesce fails we fall back to synchronous spill per key. Liam: Tests flaked on CI initially due to a racy histogram reset. Fix: switched to epoch-based counters and added deterministic test harness. Approvals: Arjun approved after race fix; Sofia approved after adding failure-mode tests. Liam approved pending perf numbers; numbers added and CI green.
